thread:
incident-bot: Paging: GPU capacity spike in prod-gpu-pool-1 — autoscaler failing to add nodes, queues growing > 10k. Paging oncall.

maya: seeing huge tail latency on /v1/generate, errors ramping. 500s -> ~15% 503s from frontends.

sam: Confirmed. Metrics: gpu-pool util ~98%, queue depth per shard 4k-6k. Autoscaler logs show repeated attempt but nodes never register.

jin: getting a stream of `Xid 79` and `cudaErrIllegalAddress` in runtime logs on a subset of nodes. suspect driver/kernel instability causing node flaps.

leo: @oncall-sre can you take initial triage? also tagging @eng-runtime for kernel/driver signal.

oncall-sre: taking it. timeline: spike started ~5098765400. I'm running `kubectl get pods -n gpu --field-selector=status.phase=Failed` now.

ops-bot: autoscaler event: `scale-up attempted (3 -> 8) but nodes failed to join within 300s. cooldown enter.`

oncall-sre: I can see 2 nodes in Failed state, kubelet logs show repeated OOMs and `CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN` on startup.

eng-runtime: pushed a small probe; attaching snippet from node logs:

```
[2025-12-03T17:30:12Z] driver: gpu0: Xid 79: GPU exception on channel 0x0001
[2025-12-03T17:30:12Z] runtime: kubelet: container restart (OOMKilled)
[2025-12-03T17:30:13Z] kernel: nvidia: GPU reset completed
```

maya: customer impact: internal SLOs show P95 latency went from 250ms to 2.3s. High-value customers receiving errors; support ticket #INC-3389 opened.

sam: autoscaler config: `max_nodes=40`, `scale_rate=+5/5m`. We're hitting node registration failure, so autoscaler is hitting limits logically but not capacity limits. Need mitigation to get effective capacity back.

jin: immediate mitigation suggestion: 1) pause new scheduling into affected GPU pool, 2) divert critical traffic to smaller-model pool (model-fallback), 3) temporarily reduce retry/backoff on frontend to avoid queue amplification.

leo: I'm doing a canary: cordon two worst nodes and drain non-critical pods.

oncall-sre: cordon/drain done for nodes gpu-12,gpu-14. Drained 120 low-priority pods -> freed ~8% capacity but driver instability persists on other nodes.

eng-runtime: hypothesis: recent kernel driver rollout 2025.11.2 may have a regression with specific GPU firmware. Rolling back to 2025.10.9 on a test node.

ops-bot: rollback job queued: `rollback-driver --version=2025.10.9 --target=gpu-pool-1 --parallel=2`.

maya: routing change: switching prod traffic rate-limited to 80% + sending 20% to model-fallback (smaller quantized models) to protect latency-sensitive flows.

sam: reduced frontend retry to single attempt for generator endpoints, TTL reduced.

eng-runtime: rollback applied to 2 nodes. After reboot they registered cleanly. No Xid entries in last 60s on those.

oncall-sre: good signal: average queue depth dropped 30% after partial rollback + traffic diversion. Still seeing sporadic OOMs on older nodes.

jin: digging into coredumps: found `kernel oops` referencing `nvidia_uvm` allocations. Might be fragmentation under heavy sustained sequences.

leo: We should scale up to dedicated reserved pool while we remediate. Sam, can you open a quick reserved-capacity request for burst? @support-team

sam: opened reserved-burst ticket RB-992, requested +10 reserved GPUs in us-west-2, ETA 15m.

ops-bot: autoscaler temporarily set `disable_scale_up=true` to avoid adding nodes that could flap while driver issue continues.

maya: customer comms draft: "We are mitigating an infrastructure issue impacting generation latency. We're diverting traffic to alternative capacity and expect restoration within 60 minutes. We'll update in 15." Approve?

jin: +1, send.

oncall-sre: handoff planned at +30m to night-shift. Current status: partial rollback successful on subset; autoscaler disabled for scale-up; reserved-burst requested; traffic diversion live; queue depth trending down but not back to normal.

eng-runtime: next actions: 1) sweep kernel driver versions, 2) run stress on node image w/ reproducer, 3) prepare full rollback plan if instability persists.

maya: logging notes and customer ticket links: INC-3389, RB-992, runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-autoscale

oncall-sre: leaving stub handoff: will be monitoring for 30m then hand to night oncall. If Xid spikes > 5/min escalate to eng-runtime pager. :white_check_mark:

sam: thanks all. adding post-incident notes and timeline to postmortem template after this stabilizes.

incident-bot: Incident updated: status=investigating -> mitigated_partial. Owners: eng-runtime, infra-oncall. Severity: Sev2.

maya: closing thread for now — continue updates in #inc-postmortem when ready. :pray:
